newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech opposition expulsions help minority govt.
newsitem.headline: Czech opposition expulsions help minority govt.

text.p: The opposition Czech Social Democrats have expelled two rebel members of parliament in a vote which gives a breathing space to the minority government of right-wing Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.

The party leadership voted on Saturday to expel Jozef Wagner, chairman of the parliamentary budget committee, and another deputy after they voted with Klaus's coalition for the 1997 state budget on Friday, the Czech news agency CTK reported.
The expulsions, which followed months of infighting in Social Democrat ranks, leaves Klaus's coalition and the three opposition parties with 99 seats in parliament each.

The party central committee called on Wagner and the other expelled deputy, Tomas Teplik, to resign from parliament. But it has no power to force them out and the two will continue to sit as independents.

The expulsions further muddy the waters of Czech politics following inconclusive lower house elections in June, when Klaus's three-party coalition narrowly lost its majority due to a strong Social Democrat performance.
Opposition parties won 101 seats in the 200-member chamber but Klaus clung to power when Zeman ruled out a coalition with the little-reformed Communists and the far-right Republicans.
Together the three opposition parties could bring down the Klaus government and next year's budget had been tipped as their first chance since a vote of confidence in July.
But Social Democrat defections let the budget through both in its first reading last month, when four deputies including Wagner voted with the government, and in Friday's third reading.
The balanced budget was passed on Friday by 99 to 96 votes.
